pages.text: Mittens was a little kitten. She lived in a cozy cottage.
pages.scene: Wide shot: Small orange tabby kitten with white paws sitting on wooden cottage floor near a fireplace. Warm golden afternoon light streaming through windows.

pages.text: Mittens liked to look for fun things. She wanted something to play with.
pages.scene: Medium shot: Mittens prowling low with bright green eyes alert, exploring under furniture in the cottage living room. Curious hunting posture.

pages.text: She looked under the bed. Nothing was there but dust.
pages.scene: Close-up: Mittens peering under a wooden bed frame, whiskers twitching, with dust particles floating in dim light underneath.

pages.text: She looked in the kitchen. Nothing but her dinner dish.
pages.scene: Medium shot: Mittens sitting disappointed next to her empty food bowl on kitchen floor tiles. Afternoon light from kitchen window.

pages.text: Then Mittens saw something odd. A button was on the wall.
pages.scene: Close-up: Mittens staring up at a small wooden button or knob protruding from the cottage wall paneling. Intrigued expression.

pages.text: She jumped up and hit the button. Something happened very fast!
pages.scene: Medium shot: Mittens leaping up with paws extended toward the wall button, mid-jump with dynamic motion. Surprised expression.

pages.text: The wall opened up! It was a hidden spot.
pages.scene: Wide shot: A secret panel in the cottage wall sliding open, revealing a dark hidden compartment. Mittens crouched low in amazement.

pages.text: Inside the hidden spot was a basket. It was very pretty.
pages.scene: Medium shot: Mittens peering into the secret compartment at a woven basket with decorative patterns. Soft mysterious lighting.

pages.text: Mittens got closer to the basket. What was in it?
pages.scene: Close-up: Mittens cautiously approaching the basket with one paw extended, whiskers forward, eyes wide with curiosity.

pages.text: She looked inside the basket. A little rabbit was sleeping!
pages.scene: Close-up: Mittens looking down into the basket at a small sleeping brown rabbit curled up on soft fabric. Gentle surprise on her face.

pages.text: The rabbit woke up and hopped out. It was very happy!
pages.scene: Medium shot: Small brown rabbit hopping out of the basket while Mittens watches with delight. Both animals showing joy and excitement.

pages.text: Now Mittens had a new friend. They played together every day.
pages.scene: Wide shot: Mittens and the rabbit playing together on the cottage floor in warm golden light. Both animals happy and energetic.

metadata.generation_prompt:
You are a master children's book author creating stories that are BOTH phonetically appropriate AND emotionally compelling.

Create a 12-page story for level C3 (Two-Syllable Closed) readers.

Concept: A kitten finds a hidden basket
Setting: a cozy cottage
Suggest a catchy title (2-4 words)

## WORD PALETTE (inspiration, not constraint)

PHONICS PATTERNS:
  VC/CV division: rab-bit, kit-ten, hap-pen, but-ton, mit-ten, sud-den
  Double consonant: better, butter, dinner, funny, happy, puppy, silly, ladder
SIGHT WORDS: ['Previous + little, something, nothing']

## CRITICAL RULE: LOGIC AND CONTINUITY

Every sentence MUST make logical sense. Check cause and effect. Check physical reality.

LOGIC ERRORS TO AVOID:
- "He got wet in the sun." (sun doesn't make you wet)
- "Now Max is not wet." (after a bath? he'd be soaking wet!)
- "He is wet and red." (why red? makes no sense)
- "The cat ran to sit." (awkward phrasing)

GOOD LOGIC:
- "Max jumped in the mud. Mud splashed on his nose!" (cause → effect)
- "Mom dried Max with a towel. Now his fur was fluffy." (action → result)
- "The pup ran fast. He wanted that ball!" (motivation → action)

CONTINUITY CHECK - Before writing each page, ask:
- What state is the character in from the previous page?
- What would logically happen next?
- Does this follow from what just happened?

If a phonics word doesn't fit naturally, DON'T USE IT.

## REQUIREMENTS

Level guidance: Chapter-style. 'The kitten was hidden in the basket. It happened so suddenly!'
- Max 12 words per sentence (STRICT - count every word!)
- 12 story pages, 2-3 short sentences each
- Use SIMPLE words from the palette - avoid multi-syllable words
- Every sentence must pass the "does this make sense?" test

VOCABULARY CHECK - these are TOO HARD for early levels:
- "washes" → use "gets" or "rubs"
- "ready" → use "set"
- "water" → ok as sight word but keep sentences short
- "towel" → ok but keep it simple

AWKWARD PHRASING TO AVOID:
- "has not got" → use "wants" or "needs"
- "can not get" → use "did not get" or restructure
- "is wet and has mud" → use "is wet with mud"
- Double negatives or clunky constructions
- Sentences that sound like grammar exercises
Write like you're talking to a child, not filling in blanks.

## VISUAL STYLE FOR THIS BAND (C)

Rich watercolor, more detailed characters and settings, dynamic compositions. Exciting, imaginative mood.

Use this style guidance for visual_style field and all scene descriptions.

## WHAT MAKES A GOOD STORY

1. CHARACTER WANT - wants something specific and clear
2. OBSTACLE - a real problem (not manufactured drama)
3. TRY-FAIL - genuine attempt that fails for a logical reason
4. RESOLUTION - satisfying and earned
5. CAUSATION - each event causes the next (not random scenes)

## OUTPUT: JSON only

```json
{{
  "title": "Story Title",
  "summary": "One sentence description",
  "characters": {{
    "char_id": {{
      "name": "Name",
      "visual_shorthand": "brief visual description",
      "distinctive_features": ["feature1", "feature2"]
    }}
  }},
  "setting_context": "Setting description",
  "visual_style": "Describe your art style based on the VISUAL STYLE section above",
  "word_list": {{"sound_out": [], "sight": [], "heart": []}},
  "pages": [
    {{
      "story_page": 1,
      "text": "Story text here.",
      "scene": "Medium shot: [WHO with visual details] [ACTION verb-ing] in [WHERE with specifics]. [Mood/lighting]."
    }}
  ],
  "reference_prompt": "[Full 9-panel reference sheet prompt - see instructions below]"
}}
```

SCENE RULES:
- WHO: Character with exact visual details from characters section
- WHERE: Specific setting with lighting/atmosphere
- WHAT: Active verb describing the action
- STATE: Show character's current physical state (wet? muddy? clean? tired?)
- Shot type: Wide/Medium/Close-up
- NEVER use negations ("no ball" makes ball appear)
- Keep scenes CLEAN - no "NO TEXT" instructions (added later)

SCENE CONTINUITY - scenes must flow like a movie:
- If character got muddy on page 4, they're STILL muddy on page 5 (unless cleaned)
- If character is in the bath, they'll be WET when they get out
- Track: location changes, character state changes, time of day
- Each scene should visually connect to the previous one

REFERENCE_PROMPT (write this LAST, after completing all pages):

```

FORMAT: Square 1:1, 3x3 grid, thin white borders between panels.

```

Use SPECIFIC details from YOUR story - actual character names, actual objects, actual settings.
